_comment: R8.1. What a trainer says before a battle, and what they say once they have lost one. Same `{"conversations": {...}}` shape as opening.json and village.json, merged onto the same table by scripts/story/dialogue_runner.gd -- a separate file so a trainer's challenge and Grandpa's briefing stay independently editable, and so test_dialogue_runner.gd's coverage of the opening's own ids is unaffected by how many trainers exist.
_comment_battle_start: The BATTLE is not an effect in here. scripts/world/trainer_npc.gd starts it when the challenge conversation closes -- the words are the challenge, and a `battle:` effect would put trainer fights inside the opening's beat machine (sequence_director.gd), which is the one state machine they are not part of.
_comment_relay: SE25. Team Tether at the relay station. The register is OFFICIOUS, not cartoonish: these are people doing a job they believe in, who think the barriers are necessary and that the player is interfering with important work. Nobody gloats, nobody monologues, and nobody threatens. They also never explain what the relay is FOR -- spec 32's ladder puts the explanation two rungs above this one, and a grunt who knew would be a grunt who tells you.
_comment_short: Two or three lines. A trainer who monologues is a trainer the player skips, and the fight is the content.

trainer_practice_challenge.speaker: Bryn
lines: You've got one at your heel and no idea what it can do yet. That's the same place everyone starts.
Two of mine, one at a time. Beat them both and you'll know something you can't be told.

trainer_practice_defeated.speaker: Bryn
lines: Both of them, and you barely stopped to think about it. Good.
I've nothing left to teach you out here. Try the folk down by the square — they don't go easy.

relay_hess_challenge.speaker: Hess
lines: Road's closed past this post. It's been closed since before you could walk it, and there's a reason for that.
You want through, you go through me first. That's procedure, not a grudge.

relay_hess_defeated.speaker: Hess
lines: Logged and reported. That's all I can do from a picket.
Go on up if you're going. You'll find people up there who outrank my opinion of you.

relay_orrin_challenge.speaker: Orrin
lines: Hess radioed. Second post, same answer — I'd rather turn you round than write you up.
You people always think a closed road is somebody being unkind. It isn't. Stand ready.

relay_orrin_defeated.speaker: Orrin
lines: Fair. I'll not pretend otherwise.
Whatever you think you'll find at the top of this road — it's work, that's all. It's just work.

relay_dell_challenge.speaker: Officer Dell
lines: Two pickets down and you walked up the service road like it was market day. Impressive. Also unacceptable.
I run this station's duty roster, not its policy. But I do keep its perimeter. Three of mine.

relay_dell_defeated.speaker: Officer Dell
lines: Beaten cleanly, at my own post. I'll not dress that up in the log.
The Captain's at the console. Say what you like to him — he's better at this part than I am.

relay_captain_challenge.speaker: Captain Vance
lines: You've come a long way to be told something simple, so I'll be plain about it: this station is necessary, and it stays.
Every road you found closed was closed on purpose, by people who weighed the cost and paid it. Your village is safe because of what we do here.
I'd rather you understood that than fought me. But I'll take the fight if that's the only language left.

relay_captain_defeated_greeting.speaker: Captain Vance
lines: The station's yours to walk through. I won't stop you, and I won't apologise for it either.
You'll take our prisoner as well, I expect. Take them. They only ever asked questions.
Ask me again when you've seen the far end of this line. I doubt either of us will enjoy the answer.

stronghold_patrol_challenge.speaker: Patrolman Verrick
lines: Nobody walks the works. That's the whole of my orders and I've never had to explain them before.
Turn round or take the fight. I'd rather you turned round -- it's a long way in and it only gets worse.

stronghold_patrol_defeated.speaker: Patrolman Verrick
lines: Fine. You're better than the orders account for.
There's a yard past the gate and someone in it who won't say that.

stronghold_courtyard_challenge.speaker: Warder Solene
lines: You saw what we pulled out of the quarry. You saw the lines going in. And you came anyway.
Three of mine. If you don't have three worth sending out, this is where you find that out.

stronghold_courtyard_defeated.speaker: Warder Solene
lines: Three, and you didn't lose one. All right.
Keeper Hald holds the shutter into the chamber approach. He won't talk to you the way I did.

stronghold_elite_challenge.speaker: Keeper Hald
lines: The shutter behind me stays down while I'm standing. That isn't a threat, it's the wiring.
The Warden doesn't want you dead. He wants you to understand. I'd rather you didn't get the chance.

stronghold_elite_defeated.speaker: Keeper Hald
lines: It's open. I can't hold it shut from the floor.
Rest your five first. He fields more than I do, and he'll wait -- he always thinks people will listen if he waits.

captain_field_challenge.speaker: Captain Halder
lines: Far as the pasture, no further. That's the posting, and I've kept it eleven years.
You've seen what walks in off the high ground when a fence goes down. I've buried the difference.
No trick to this ground and none to mine. Whoever's strongest walks off it.
Sigil's on my belt and it stays there unless you take it properly. Bring them out.

captain_field_defeated.speaker: Captain Halder
lines: Clean. No arguing with clean.
Take it — that's the rule and I'd not be worth the badge if I bent it.
Vess is up the road yet, if you haven't already met her wind.

captain_ridge_challenge.speaker: Captain Vess
lines: Careful. Crosswind on this shoulder has taken better-footed than you off it.
People call the ridge line cruel. It's a wall, and a wall is the kindest thing we've built up here.
You got up here already breathing hard, I'd wager. Good — whatever's left in your five is what fights mine.
Mine fly it every day. Let's see yours.

captain_ridge_defeated.speaker: Captain Vess
lines: You read the gusts. Most don't bother.
The Ridge Sigil, then. I'd sooner it went to someone who watches the sky.
Oreth's down in the draw, if the river didn't have him first. He's the patient one — don't let him tire you into a mistake.

captain_riverwatch_challenge.speaker: Captain Oreth
lines: Riverwatch. We keep the low ground, and the low ground is where everything ends up.
You'll think the barriers are what's wrong here. Stand a season in this draw and you'll thank whoever set them.
Three of mine. Not all one type — you'll want a plan, not a favourite.

captain_riverwatch_defeated.speaker: Captain Oreth
lines: A plan, then. Good.
However many you're carrying now, that's one more. The Hall approach reads all three or it reads none — no bargaining with a lock.
Go on up. I hope you're right about whatever you think is in there.

patrol_ridgeline_challenge.speaker: Tether Patrol
lines: Ridge road's not on the closed list, but that doesn't mean you're waved through.
Halder and Vess get the paperwork. I get the ones who wander off it.

patrol_ridgeline_defeated.speaker: Tether Patrol
lines: Fine. You're not the one I was posted to stop anyway.
Watch the ruin overhead — something's denned in it that isn't ours.

_comment_stronghold: SG38. The three stronghold gauntlet trainers. Same two-or-three-line rule as everyone above -- the fight is the content. What they say is Sec33's Warden read down the ladder: none of them is gloating, all three would rather the player stopped, and Keeper Hald says outright that the Warden wants to be understood rather than obeyed. None of them reveals what the machine is; that is SG40's, inside the stronghold and nowhere earlier.
_comment_captains: SF34. The three regional captains. Spec §35-§36's rule for Team Tether officers is the one thing these lines exist to carry: they are NOT sneering villains, they believe the barriers protect people, and each of them has a specific regional reason to believe it. Nobody explains the Rifts here -- §32's reveal ladder keeps the explanation for the stronghold, and a captain who monologued the plot would spend it three rungs early. Two or three lines each, same as every other trainer in this file.
